survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The document describes the PISA 2000 international database and how to analyse it using complex survey design features. It specifies that sampling weights must be applied to compensate for unequal selection probabilities of students within schools, and it identifies the final student weight as W_FSTUWT (with additional country adjustment factors for cross-country comparability). For variance estimation, it provides Fay’s balanced repeated replication (80 replicates) and indicates that the corresponding replicate weights (W_FSTR1–W_FSTR80) should be used to compute sampling variances. It also explains that when analysing mathematics or science using reading weights, analysts must apply domain-specific weight adjustment factors to avoid over/under-representing students assigned to the special education booklet.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a technical database manual rather than an empirical study estimating a model with a missing-data strategy. The manual explains how missing responses are coded in the dataset (e.g., item non-response, multiple/invalid responses, not applicable, and not reached items), but it does not specify an imputation or deletion rule for missing questionnaire/test variables in statistical analyses. Therefore, missing_data_handling is not reported as an analysis procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The manual defines which records are included in the PISA 2000 international database: all students who attended one of the two test sessions, plus students who only attended the questionnaire session if they provided responses to the father’s or mother’s occupation questions (questions 8–11). It excludes students reported as not eligible, no longer at school, excluded for physical/mental/linguistic reasons, absent on the test day, who refused to participate, and students from schools where less than 25% of sampled eligible students participated in the testing sessions. At the school level, it includes all participating schools where at least 25% of sampled eligible students were assessed, regardless of whether the school questionnaire was returned.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a technical manual for the PISA 2000 international database rather than an empirical research paper. It describes the rotated test design used to assess 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics, and science, with different booklets covering different domain combinations and a special education booklet used in a limited set of countries. It explains the structure of the downloadable files (student, school, questionnaire, and item/test data) and how missing data are represented via specific missing codes (item non-response, invalid responses, not applicable, and not reached items). For performance measurement, it details the availability of both weighted likelihood estimates and plausible values, recommending plausible values for population-level statistics and describing how to analyse them using WesVar® or SAS®/SPSS® with Fay’s balanced repeated replication. It also provides guidance for cross-country comparability through country adjustment factors and for domain-specific weight adjustments when using reading weights for mathematics/science analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to an OECD technical database manual, not an empirical study estimating predictive models. As a result, there is no student-level analytic sample size reported for a specific research question, no ML algorithms trained, and no model performance metrics or target-variable effects to tabulate. The manual’s value is methodological: it specifies how to construct and analyse PISA 2000 variables (weights, plausible values, replicates, and coding rules) so that downstream empirical studies can produce valid population estimates.
